concerns.message: The new sail-and-dock approach (item 8: from a waypoint 3 tiles out on the dock's axis, turn until the HUD heading points at the dock, then hold ahead + E and let the shore stop the ship) only docks when the ship is almost exactly on the dock's column. sailTo stops within one tile (256 sub-units), and from more than about 43 sub-units off the axis the rounded bearing to the dock is already a diagonal heading. Traced through step.ts on the harbour map in simulation.test.ts (land west of the dock, sea east): (a) on a diagonal heading the ship hits the shore, is blocked on only one axis, is not aground, and slides along the coast with its speed still at maxSpeed, above dockMaxSpeed, so it never moors and slides out of reach. (b) Even heading straight north, a lateral offset over 48 sub-units (tile half 128 minus hull half 80) grounds the hull on the land tile beside the dock. The ship stops there, but hullPathIsClear to the berth crosses that land tile's corner (the case 'does not moor across a corner' tests), so dockInReach fails and the ship stays stuck. The simulation test the plan cites covers only the exactly aligned case (shipAt(dock.tileX, dock.tileY + 2, 48)).
concerns.consequence: sail-and-dock fails whenever sailTo stops the ship off the dock's axis toward the land side. That depends on load and timing, so the flake this plan is meant to remove comes back: --repeat-each=5 fails or passes by luck, and the verifier's browser check fails intermittently. Fix before workers start: approach from the dock's open-water side with a heading tilted toward the land beside the dock (for a south dock with land to the west: last waypoint at dock.tileX+1 or +2, dock.tileY+3, heading one or two units west of north). The ship then slides into the corner of land north of the dock and the land beside it, runs aground on both axes inside the dock tile, and moors with E held, whatever its offset. Choose the map dock for that geometry (open sea on one side, land on the other), assert it in the test, and add a simulation unit test for a sweep of lateral offsets.

concerns.message: decisions.md contradicts itself. One bullet says the sail-and-dock test 'brakes until the dock hint reads "Press E to dock", then taps E'. The 'Corrected after design challenge attempt 2' bullet and task item 8 say hold ahead + E with no timed taps and no brake at a stop.
concerns.consequence: A worker who reads decisions.md as authoritative may build the tap-based approach, which item 8 forbids. That costs a review round.

concerns.message: The out-of-sight row placed 'through the hub' conflicts with midline shoal walls if the horizontal wall sits on the hub's row. That row is open only inside the ±5-tile gap, less than the 12–13 tiles between the ships plus room to turn around and coast. sailTo also turns about through a circle roughly 3 tiles across (turning radius about 1.55 tiles at 39 sub-units per step), always to the same side (left for an exact reversal).
concerns.consequence: The test can't be written on the layout that passes the validators, which forces the map to be redesigned after validation (the case item 9 warns about). Plan the row parallel to the horizontal wall, offset by at least 3–4 tiles, crossing the vertical wall's gap, with turning room on the side sailTo turns to.

concerns.message: 'A hub disc of radius SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES / 2, so any two ships inside it can see each other' holds for tile centres only. Ships sit anywhere inside their tile, so two ships on tiles at opposite edges of the inclusive disc can be slightly more than 10 tiles apart.
concerns.consequence: A unit test or doc line that asserts mutual sight at the disc's extreme positions fails or is misleading. Either phrase it as tile centres, or make the disc exclusive or shrink it by about one tile.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Keep the plan and change only how sail-and-dock docks. Use a corner of the island's shore instead of relying on exact alignment: pick a dock with land on one side of its row and open sea on the other. Put the last waypoint 1–2 tiles toward the open side and 3 tiles out, and have the test turn to a fixed heading tilted toward the land side (for example 47 or 46 for a south dock with land to the west) rather than 'toward the dock'. Then hold ahead + E. The ship either grounds against the land north of the dock or slides along it into the land beside the dock, stopping inside the dock tile with a clear path, and moors. It works for any lateral offset within about a tile and any load, and needs no new mechanics or tap timing. For the map, generate the .tmj from one quadrant of an ASCII sketch copied into all four, so the travel-time, density and hub checks need tuning only once.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Before writing the browser test, add a throwaway vitest case next to the 'docks a ship driven into its dock with ahead held' test. Using the new shipTuning on the harbour map, start the ship at berth.y + 3 tiles with lateral offsets from -256 to +256 in steps of 16 sub-units. Give it (a) the rounded bearing to the dock as heading, and (b) a fixed heading tilted toward the land beside the dock, starting from the open side. Run sailFor with helm(0, 1, INTERACT_BUTTON) for 80 steps and count how many runs end moored. This takes minutes and shows whether 'point at the dock' works (I expect it fails for about half the offsets) and whether the corner approach docks at every offset.
